_note: Anant Raj is the flagship execution case in the brief. Nothing here is read from a filing: every figure is a research note or press figure, tagged SECONDARY throughout. No financial statements have been read, so this page deliberately carries no margins, no returns and no cost stack. It is a capacity and delivery page only, and it says so.
role: Real estate developer pivoting to colocation data centres

ladder.definition: Target IT load by Fiscal 2032, against roughly 2.1 billion dollars of stated capex. A plan, not an asset.
IT load described as operational across the two live campuses, Manesar and Panchkula.
Colocation completely handed over to customers. The remainder was still in the handover process.

ladderSource.label: Blueprint research note, BharatAI Infra Scope, quoting Value Research: only 8 MW of colocation had been completely handed over, while the rest was still in the handover process, and operational capacity is not the same as handed over capacity. A separate campus level record puts Anant Raj Cloud at 307 MW announced against 21 MW live, which disagrees with the 28 MW figure. Both are recorded and neither is averaged.

a.source: Blueprint research note, Manesar 21 plus Panchkula 7

b.source: data/campuses.json, the figure recorded before the annual report was cited

conflict.note: A seven megawatt disagreement on a 28 megawatt estate is a quarter of the number. Until a filing settles it the higher figure is carried, and the disagreement is shown rather than resolved.

notRead: The audited financial statements inside the annual report, and the notes to them

annualReport._note: The first Anant Raj document opened in this repository. It was read for capacity and for the audit opinion only. The financial statements sit in the same file and have not been read, which is why the risk register still carries no row for cash conversion or the balance sheet.

IT load actually operational, at Manesar, including 0.5 MW of cloud services.
The operational figure less the cloud services inside it, which is a different business sold to different customers.

Named in the same sentence as the additional Manesar load, and in the same state.

compositionSource.label: Anant Raj Limited annual report FY2024-25, corporate overview highlights and the management discussion, which state the same three parts in the same words in two places.

risks.gradingNote: Severity and likelihood are analyst gradings, not the company's. A magnitude marked measured is derived from the figures recorded for this name, and those figures come from a research note rather than from a filing. Derived is not the same as filed, and each row says which it is.
risks.unevidencedNote: One document would close every empty pillar. The audited financial statements and the notes to accounts sit inside the annual report for FY2024-25, and only its capacity pages and its audit opinion are cited here. Without those statements there is no revenue quality, no cash conversion, no governance and no valuation to grade, and a row written anyway would be a grade with nothing behind it.

rows.risk: Capacity the company calls operational is not capacity a customer has taken, and the drop between the two is hidden inside a figure already described as operational.
rows.mitigant: The remainder is described as still in the handover process rather than as stalled, so some of it is a queue rather than a failure.
rows.note: This is the same gap the Sify pages call built against sold, in a different vocabulary. Neither company uses the other's words, and nothing in either set of words warns a reader which rung is being quoted.

source.label: Blueprint research note, BharatAI Infra Scope, quoting Value Research on colocation handed over against capacity called operational

rows.risk: The announced target is more than thirty times what has actually been handed over, and the schedule to it runs to Fiscal 2032.
rows.mitigant: A long horizon is not by itself a broken promise. The target is dated, so it can be graded later rather than argued about now.
rows.note: The site does not grade this claim yet, because its horizon has not passed. It is recorded so that it can be.

source.label: Blueprint research note, BharatAI Infra Scope, target IT load by Fiscal 2032

rows.risk: Two sources give two different figures for operational capacity, and the disagreement is a quarter of the estate.
rows.mitigant: Both figures are recorded here and neither is averaged, so a reader sees the disagreement rather than a number that hides it.
rows.note: This is a disclosure risk rather than a board governance one. Nothing about the board, the auditor or related parties has been read, so the governance pillar stays empty rather than borrowing this row.

source.label: Blueprint research note against the separately recorded campus level figure

rows.risk: The target carries a stated capital cost in billions of dollars, against a balance sheet nobody here has opened.
rows.mitigant: None stated. Funding, gearing and the capital already committed sit in the audited financial statements inside the annual report.
rows.note: The magnitude here is the size of the programme, not an assessment of whether it can be funded. That assessment needs the statements this page does not have.

source.label: Blueprint research note, BharatAI Infra Scope, stated capex against the Fiscal 2032 target

rows.risk: A real estate developer is building and operating colocation, which is a different business with different customers, different uptime obligations and a different cost base.
rows.mitigant: Land and construction capability are genuine transferable advantages, and they are the two things a pure colocation entrant usually lacks.
rows.note: Not measured, and marked as such. There is no figure that captures whether a pivot is being executed well, and inventing one would be worse than grading it openly.

source.label: Blueprint research note, BharatAI Infra Scope, real estate to data centre pivot
